source_text: Ὅτι οὐ δεῖ ὑπηρέτας ἔχειν ἐν τῷ διακονικῷ, καὶ ἄπτεσθαι τῶν ἱερῶν σκευῶν.
thought_title: Servants must not handle sacred vessels
orientation: The Council of Laodicea is issuing its own decrees, and this canon restricts the role of servants in the sanctuary.
pass_a_gloss: That it is not necessary for servants to be in the diaconicon, and to touch the sacred vessels.

choices.why: The brief identifies ὑπηρέται as attendants who guard doors and handle vessels but may not bless or distribute; 'servants' is the plain English equivalent.
The source uses the technical term for the room where sacred vessels are kept; 'diaconicon' preserves the specific liturgical space.
The phrase refers to the consecrated liturgical vessels; 'sacred vessels' is the standard English rendering.
The impersonal δεῖ with οὐ expresses prohibition; 'it is not necessary' keeps the impersonal force of the Greek.

pass_b_english: Servants are not to be stationed in the diaconicon or to touch the sacred vessels.
